items.title: Eddie Metz Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, October 3, 2015
items.q: I was working in Allentown with a guy named Parke Frankenfield who was big in the Lehigh Valley area... a steady Friday and Saturday with this quartet.

ctx.x: And I think I read in some of your bio information that they eventually cut back on their music?

I went to Florida in 1985. I’d gotten married and had a kid. P.J. was born in October of ’84. Sorry October of ’85. And we were living in Flemington, New Jersey at the time. And I was working in Allentown with a guy named Parke Frankenfield who was big in the Lehigh Valley area. Again, a band organizer who had a big band, a small group, and a steady Friday and Saturday with this quartet. And he played keyboards at the time, although he was mostly a trombone player. A jack of all trades. He played everything. And…

had worked around town and played at Rosie O’Grady’s and started doing conventions, got to know the contractors in town. Disney had 400 full time musicians there at the time, and now, 30 years later, they’re down to 65 I think, full time musicians. They’ve just cut a lot of the entertainment. As I understand it, just as I moved to town, Operations, Disney World Operations had taken over entertainment, and they knew nothing about entertainment. They are wondering why are all these people sitting around in between…
